introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics With Statistics, Paper 3 (0770/3), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2019. Time allowed: THREE HOURS.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae and tables produced by the GCE Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Electronic calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.
enonce_intro_markdown:
The marks obtained by 100 candidates in an examination are summarized in the distribution below.

| Marks, $(x)$ | 10-19 | 20-29 | 30-39 | 40-49 | 50-59 | 60-69 | 70-79 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency, $(f)$ | 3 | 20 | 35 | 25 | 7 | 5 | 5 |
incertitudes: Question 7 : les points imprimés sont (2, 3, 4, 2), soit 11 et non 13 : quatre valeurs pour cinq blocs ((i)(a), (i)(b), (ii), (iii)(a), (iii)(b)). Lecture retenue : 2 pour (i)(a), 3 pour (i)(b), 4 pour (ii) et 2 pour (iii) ; ce dernier 2 est porté par iii.a, iii.b n'ayant pas de points propres. Le total imprimé n'est pas corrigé : il manque probablement 2 points (écart d'impression à vérifier).

Question 7 (i)(b) : l'écart type est calculé avec le diviseur $n = 100$ (13.67) ; avec $n - 1$ on obtiendrait 13.74. Les marques sont des entiers : classes 10-19, ..., de limites réelles 9.5, 19.5, ... ; la moyenne utilise les centres 14.5, 24.5, ...

Question 7 (ii), (iii) : la courbe est à tracer par l'élève (aucune figure imprimée) ; le corrigé donne les points (limites supérieures, fréquences cumulées). Les lectures sont des estimations : (iii)(a) environ 30 candidats (28 si la lecture se fait en abscisse 45 au lieu de 44.5) ; (iii)(b) environ 59.5, soit 60 en notes entières.

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) The standard deviation of the marks
questions.corrige_markdown:
Using the totals of the table above, $\sum f = 100$, $\sum fx^2 = 173145$ and $\bar{x} = 39.3$:

$$\sigma^2 = \frac{\sum fx^2}{\sum f} - \bar{x}^2 = \frac{173145}{100} - 39.3^2 = 1731.45 - 1544.49 = 186.96$$

$$\sigma = \sqrt{186.96} = 13.67$$

**Standard deviation $\approx 13.7$ marks** (13.67; the whole class of 100 is treated as the population, divisor $n = 100$).

questions.enonce_markdown: **(ii)** Draw the cumulative frequency curve for this distribution.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The marks are whole numbers, so the upper class boundaries are 19.5, 29.5, ..., 79.5. Cumulative frequencies:

| Upper boundary | 9.5 | 19.5 | 29.5 | 39.5 | 49.5 | 59.5 | 69.5 | 79.5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cumulative frequency | 0 | 3 | 23 | 58 | 83 | 90 | 95 | 100 |

**Drawing.** Plot the marks on the horizontal axis (for example 1 cm for 10 marks, from 0 to 80) and the cumulative frequency on the vertical axis (for example 1 cm for 10 candidates, from 0 to 100). Plot the points $(9.5, 0)$, $(19.5, 3)$, $(29.5, 23)$, $(39.5, 58)$, $(49.5, 83)$, $(59.5, 90)$, $(69.5, 95)$, $(79.5, 100)$ and join them with a smooth S-shaped curve (an ogive), which rises steeply between 20 and 50 and flattens after 60. Label the axes and give the graph a title.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**(iii)** Using the curve drawn in (ii), determine

(a) the number of candidates who will pass the exam if the pass mark is 45.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A candidate passes with a mark of 45 or more, that is, with a mark above 44.5 on the continuous scale. Read the cumulative frequency at $x = 44.5$ on the curve. Between $(39.5, 58)$ and $(49.5, 83)$ the curve is nearly straight, so

$$CF(44.5) \approx 58 + \frac{44.5 - 39.5}{10} \times (83 - 58) = 58 + 12.5 = 70.5$$

About 70 or 71 candidates scored below 45, so

$$\text{number passing} \approx 100 - 70.5 = 29.5 \approx 30$$

**About 30 candidates pass** (a graph reading of 28 to 30 is acceptable; reading at $x = 45$ gives about 28).

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) the least mark a candidate must earn to be awarded an A grade if the top $10\%$ of the class is to earn an A.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The top $10\%$ of 100 candidates are the 10 best candidates. The lowest of these is above the 90th candidate, so read the mark at cumulative frequency $100 - 10 = 90$ on the curve.

From the table, $CF(59.5) = 90$ exactly: 90 candidates scored 59 or less, so the 10 best scored 60 or more.

**The least mark for an A grade is about $59.5$, that is $60$ marks.**
